leads.title: Wootz crucible steel in South India
leads.where: Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Sri Lanka
leads.why: A fully molten, uniform high-carbon steel, traded west as ingots for the blades later called Damascus, and the puzzle that drove European steel research around 1800.
leads.verify: Find the earliest dated crucible-steel production sites (Kodumanal, Mel-siruvalur) and how secure the dating is. Relate this to the Central Asian crucible steel already in the dataset (Merv) and to Huntsman's separately devised crucible steel at Sheffield in the 1740s.

wootz steel origins South India archaeology Ranganathan

leads.title: Lost-wax casting in pre-Columbian Colombia
leads.where: Cauca valley, Caribbean lowlands and highlands of Colombia
leads.why: Goldsmiths of the northern Andes reached lost-wax casting on their own, using stingless-bee wax and gold-copper alloys, and the technique passed through the Isthmus to Mexico.
leads.verify: The date is uncertain. Find the earliest securely dated lost-wax castings in Colombia or Ecuador and the cultures responsible, and trace the dated spread into Panama, Costa Rica and Mesoamerica.
search: earliest lost-wax casting Colombia pre-Columbian goldwork date
pre-Hispanic metallurgy Colombia tumbaga lost wax origins Museo del Oro

leads.title: Lost-wax bronze casting at Igbo-Ukwu
leads.why: Castings of extreme delicacy in local leaded bronze begin the West African tradition continued at Ife and Benin.
leads.verify: Confirm the radiocarbon dates, the evidence that the metal came from local ores, and the technical features that set these castings apart from North African work. Report what scholars conclude on whether the technique was invented locally or stimulated from across the Sahara.

origins of lost-wax casting West Africa

leads.title: Patio-process silver amalgamation in New Spain
leads.why: Cold amalgamation made low-grade ores pay, and the silver of Mexico and Potosi that it released became the money of world trade from Seville to Manila and China.
leads.verify: Confirm Bartolome de Medina's role and date, what was known of amalgamation in Europe beforehand, and when and how the process was adapted at Potosi with Huancavelica mercury. Note the indigenous Andean smelting (huayrachina wind furnaces) it displaced.

leads.title: Wood-pulp paper in Saxony
leads.why: Paper from trees ended the rag shortage and made newsprint, cheap books, schoolbooks, packaging and cardboard possible on a mass scale.
leads.verify: Confirm Keller's groundwood process and Voelter's commercialisation, and Charles Fenerty's independent work in Nova Scotia (1844). Lay out the chemical pulping processes that followed (soda, sulfite, kraft) and judge whether kraft pulping deserves its own record.

leads.title: Phenol-formaldehyde resin (Bakelite) in New York
leads.why: The first fully synthetic plastic gave the electrical and motor industries a mouldable insulator and opened the age of materials designed from chemicals.
leads.verify: Confirm Baekeland's 1907 heat-and-pressure patent and first production, and how it differed from earlier semi-synthetic plastics made from cellulose (Parkesine, celluloid), which deserve a record of their own. The dataset has a Bakelite radio cabinet as an instance; this is the parent capability.

concepts.name: Crucible steel
concepts.summary: Making homogeneous high-carbon steel by melting iron with carbon in sealed crucibles.

concepts.name: Lost-wax casting
concepts.summary: Casting metal in a mould formed around a wax model that is melted out before pouring.

concepts.name: Phenol-formaldehyde resin
concepts.summary: A fully synthetic plastic made by condensing phenol with formaldehyde and setting it hard under heat and pressure.

concepts.name: Silver amalgamation
concepts.summary: Extracting silver from crushed low-grade ore at scale by reacting it with mercury and salts.

concepts.name: Wood-pulp paper
concepts.summary: Making paper from wood reduced to fibre by grinding or chemical cooking, in place of rags.
